items.prompt:
Weather is
A) what the air is like at a time and place
B) a type of rock
C) a fossil
D) a kind of animal
items.answer: A) what the air is like at a time and place

steps: Weather includes temperature, rain, wind, and clouds.

items.prompt:
In many places, summer is usually
A) colder than winter
B) warmer than winter
C) the same as winter
D) always snowy

steps: Summer is typically warmer than winter.

items.prompt:
We use tables and graphs of weather to
A) see seasonal patterns easily
B) hide the data
C) change the weather
D) stop the seasons

steps: Tables and graphs make patterns clear.

items.prompt:
If spring usually has more rain, you should expect spring to be
A) dry
B) rainy
C) snowy only
D) windy only

A table of rainy days per month can help describe
A) the typical weather of each season
B) the price of rain
C) the names of clouds only
D) nothing
items.answer: A) the typical weather of each season

steps: Grouping months into seasons shows seasonal weather.

items.prompt:
If winter is almost always colder each year, next winter will likely be
A) hot
B) cold
C) rainy only
D) windy only

steps: The repeating pattern suggests next winter will be cold.

items.prompt:
A temperature graph shows summer is warmer than winter because
A) the summer values are higher than the winter ones
B) the graph is colorful
C) winter is not shown
D) the graph is random
items.answer: A) the summer values are higher than the winter ones

steps: Higher summer values show it is warmer.

items.prompt:
How is weather different from a single rainy day?
A) There is no difference
B) Weather patterns describe what is typical over time, not just one day
C) A rainy day lasts a year
D) Weather is only in summer
items.answer: B) Weather patterns describe what is typical over time, not just one day

steps: A pattern is the usual weather over time, not one event.
